normalized.title: HIGH-PRECISION MECHANISM FOR ON-SKY OPTICAL BEAM DIVERGENCE ADJUSTMENT (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.080) - EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
normalized.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a mechanism for an optical ground station that can adjust the beam's divergence during the link sessionwithout link interruption and whilst maintaining the optical pointing accuracy.TargetedImprovements:To enable dynamic adjustment of the beam divergence without needing optical realignment. This will enable real-time optimisation of the link based onthe elevation angle and the turbulence conditions. Eventually, integrating the beacon capabilities with the communications beam.Description: Alignment of the optical system at an optical ground station is usually needed before a link session, especially if the optical configuration (beam divergence)has changed. Links to Low-Earth Orbit are highly dynamic, ranging for very small elevation angles up to zenith, and atmospheric turbulence conditionsevolving during a link session. It is essential that for links targeting optical feeder applications the ground-space connectivity must be maintained.Furthermore, ground-to-space links usually make use of a beacon during the acquisition phase. For these reasons, developing a mechanism that allowsfor real-time beam-divergence adjustment without the need to re-align the optical components is considered very useful.Some of the off-the-shelf components used in optical ground stations are limited in accuracy and optical power, and therefore not suitable for an on-skyreal-time adjustment of the beam divergence. This activity shall evaluate the state-of-the-art of mechanisms, with their limitations on accuracy, precisionand maximum supported power. The design and development of an engineering model shall demonstrate the capabilities of the mechanism. This goalcan be achieved either in the laboratory with realistic interfaces or at an optical ground station.

normalized.title: S3-CL-06 SECURE AUTONOMOUS DISPOSAL INTERFACE SAFETY MODULE - REISSUED
normalized.description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

normalized.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

normalized.title: SOFTWARE UPDATES SMS, MATERIAL AND LORENTZ - EXPRO+
normalized.description: The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains:            SMS scanner control software.            LORENTZ scanner control software.            CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. Maintaining compatibility withcommercial operating systems, hardware drivers and measurement instruments is therefore an essential part of maintaining the operational capability of the Antenna Laboratory. As several ESA facilities depend on the availability, reliability and traceability of measurement data,particular attention must be given to configuration control, software version management, measurement file compatibility and preservation of laboratory know-how. The software shall therefore be maintained as an operational laboratory asset rather than as a standalone development project.- Objective(s) of the ActivityThe objective of the activity is to ensure the continuous operation, maintenance, evolution and long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software systems, while preserving compatibility with existing facilities, measurement workflows and historical measurement data.

normalized.title: PRESERVATION ASSETS OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE SERVICE (PAOM-SER)
normalized.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.
